scope: Bounded exact-prefix-splicing investigation; no novelty or comprehensive literature claim.

sources.title: A Linear-Time Algorithm for Testing the Truth of Certain Quantified Boolean Formulas
sources.locator: Theorem 1, printed page 122; implication construction, printed page 121
sources.provenance: Full primary text checked in Phase 4; used here only for the ordinary 2-SAT criterion.
sources.not_attributed: The splicing recognizer and its gate-size bound are manual constructions here.

bounded_new_search: A search for min/max bottleneck Floyd recurrences was used only as background. No additional external theorem is assumed by the gate-count argument.
manual_arguments: Exact splice inner cost is the union of the input cones plus at most 2m+4 gates.
Prefix/suffix matching lengths characterize existence of a cut.
Earliest implication-edge activation times and min/max closure recover first inconsistent prefixes.
Unsigned min/max circuits yield O(binomial(m,k)^2*(m+1)*(N+2^(3k))) gates.
Adding exact center splices connects the old noisy family without accepting a NO instance in the stated regime.
Counting centers, cuts and Hamming balls bounds all accepting subcube dimensions by O(N^beta/log N).
A low-coordinate parity remains a missed YES table at distance at least N/4 from every exact splice.
limits: Exact splices of centers, not arbitrary noisy splices or iterated closure.
No claim of a full internal-oracle barrier.
No inference that the construction is novel from the bounded search.
